- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for potential rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3%.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid over-optimism.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “neutral” or “negative” patterns, model underperforms; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for lagged sentiment effects.
